transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Sparrow AI), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Samir Kaur (Infra), Lina Gomez (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery about Redwood PLG quickstart. Sparrow AI wants to prototype a chat assistant and an embeddings pipeline, lowest time-to-first-token, evaluate costs and whether they'll need Dedicated or Private later.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intros then dive into how Redwood's quickstart works and what the free credits look like.
00:12 Jordan Lee: cool yeah, thanks Alex. we have limited time, quick context — we're building a conversational assistant for our analytics UI, looking at both hosted and eventually dedicated for latency.
00:22 Maya Patel: great, quick question on time-to-first-token — from sign-up to sending first request, how long should that take?
00:30 Alex Chen: in our PLG flow you can get an API key and send a request in under five minutes. if you use the SDK quickstart it's basically pip install redwood, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, and run the example, so yeah minutes. sometimes SSO provisioning adds —
00:45 Priya Singh: mmh, and the free credits, how do those apply? are they per account or org-scoped?
00:52 Alex Chen: free credits are org-level for self-serve signups; we'll top-up a developer account to test generation and embeddings. for larger POCs we can issue additional sandbox credits via AE.
01:05 Samir Kaur: infra question — if we start on hosted, and later want dedicated with VPC, how seamless is switching? downtimes?
01:15 Maya Patel: good one — we route by model pinning and deployment policies so you can start on hosted and pin to a dedicated deployment later; typical migration is config-only, no model conversion needed. there may be brief cutovers in traffic routing but can do canary rollout to avoid downtime.
01:34 Jordan Lee: ok that's helpful. what's the difference in latency/cost if we go hosted vs dedicated? we expect a P95 latency target of <120ms for short prompts.
01:44 Maya Patel: depends on model size and batching. hosted shared capacity has variable tails during peak; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and tighter SLOs. cost per token on dedicated can be lower at scale because you commit capacity. caching and prefix KV cache also help reduce token count and latency for repeated contexts.
02:02 Priya Singh: are there pre-built policies for autoscaling? we have bursty traffic and don't want outages.
02:08 Alex Chen: yes, Dedicated supports autoscale with burst capacity options; you can set thresholds based on concurrency or queue length. for PLG early stages we recommend hosted + request-level rate limits until traffic patterns are known.
02:25 Lina Gomez: security — SOC2? SSO? audit logs?
02:29 Maya Patel: Redwood is SOC2 compliant and supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) with role-based access. we also have audit logs, per-route tracing in the console, and integrations with KMS for customer-managed keys. note: in hosted we offer encryption-at-rest and you can opt for BYOK with Private deployments.
02:52 Samir Kaur: about data residency — can we keep logs out of public clouds?
02:56 Alex Chen: for strict residency and air-gapped we have Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). otherwise hosted has region controls and retention settings.
03:07 Jordan Lee: great. about models: do you host open models or proprietary ones?
03:12 Maya Patel: we host a curated catalog of open models and redwood-verified profiles; customers can choose quantized variants for cost/perf tradeoffs. we also support function/tool calling and streaming for chat UX.
03:26 Priya Singh: any gotchas on SDKs? we use python and node.
03:30 Alex Chen: official SDKs for python and node, plus curl examples. quickstart repo includes an embeddings notebook too. typical time-to-first-token with the SDK is under 5 minutes if you have the key; with SSO provisioning (enterprise) it's more like hours depending on your SSO team.
03:48 Jordan Lee: pricing view — can you share per-token and embedding pricing?
03:52 Alex Chen: yes, we'll send the self-serve pricing sheet; hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; we can model spend for your expected qps.
04:05 Priya Singh: curious about latency benchmarks — can you run a sample POC with our prompt set?
04:10 Maya Patel: yes, we usually do a sandbox account and run a 50k-100k token benchmark to estimate P95/P99 and cost. we can do that as part of a short POC — we'll need your prompt set and some traffic profile.
04:22 Jordan Lee: okay, what's typical lead time to get a sandbox account with free credits and run the benchmark?
04:27 Alex Chen: we can onboard self-serve in minutes; for the sandbox with additional credits and whitelisted IPs, AE/SE can provision within 1-2 business days.
04:37 Samir Kaur: do you support customer-managed KMS in hosted?
04:40 Maya Patel: hosted can integrate with external KMS for key wrapping in some tiers; for full BYOK we recommend Private.
04:47 Lina Gomez: will we hit any compliance issues during a POC? we handle sensitive customer PII.
04:52 Maya Patel: we recommend redaction and minimal retention for PII in initial tests; we can also run the POC inside Private if required, but usually customers start in hosted with retention turned off and limited logs.
05:07 Jordan Lee: okay next steps?
05:09 Alex Chen: i'll send the quickstart link + free credits instructions and the pricing sheet. Maya will schedule a technical deep dive next week to set up the sandbox and run the benchmark. Jordan to send prompt set and expected qps.
05:20 Priya Singh: sounds good. thanks everyone.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches — product name sometimes recorded as Redwood Serve or Redwood Dedicated spelled Redwood Dedic8ted. Speakers overlap slightly at 01:05 and 04:37.

End of transcript.
